frame: Engine frame: +x to the engine's right (viewed from the front), +y up, +z forward toward the propeller. Origin at the crankcase centre.
note: anchor = where the label and fly-to point sit on the built-in trainer engine. anchors.<assetId> overrides it for another asset (a scan or a glTF); write those with the calibration tool (press K).

parts.name: Cylinders
parts.description: Four air-cooled cylinders, two on each side of the crankcase. Finned barrels and heads shed heat into the cooling air; compression is checked cylinder by cylinder.

parts.name: Spark plugs
parts.description: Two plugs per cylinder, top and bottom, each fed by a different magneto, so one failed circuit still leaves a spark in every cylinder.

parts.name: Ignition harness
parts.description: Shielded high-tension leads that carry each magneto's output to its spark plugs. Chafing, cracked insulation and loose terminals are the usual findings.

parts.name: Magnetos
parts.description: Two engine-driven magnetos on the rear accessory case. Each generates its own ignition current, independent of the aircraft electrical system, and fires one plug in every cylinder.

sources.section: Reciprocating Engine Ignition System Maintenance & Inspection

parts.name: Oil filter
parts.description: Full-flow spin-on filter on the accessory case. At an oil change it is opened and the pleated element examined for metal that would point to internal wear.

parts.name: Oil sump
parts.description: The oil reservoir under the crankcase of this wet-sump engine. Its drain plug and suction screen are checked for metal particles and foreign matter.

parts.name: Exhaust system
parts.description: Down-stacks from each cylinder into collectors and a muffler shrouded by a heat exchanger. Cracks here are a fire and carbon-monoxide hazard, so it gets close attention.

sources.section: Reciprocating Engine Exhaust System Maintenance Practices

parts.name: Induction system and air filter
parts.description: Filtered air box at the front of the engine feeding the intake tubes to each cylinder. Leaks or a clogged filter change how the engine breathes.

parts.name: Engine mount and vibration isolators
parts.description: Welded tube frame tying the engine to the firewall through rubber vibration isolators. Look for cracked welds, looseness and perished rubber.

parts.name: Cooling baffles
parts.description: Sheet-metal baffles and rubber seals that force cooling air down through the cylinder fins instead of around them. A torn seal or bent baffle can overheat a cylinder.

parts.name: Crankcase
parts.description: The split case that carries the crankshaft and the cylinders. The engine section is checked here for oil, fuel and other leaks and for loose or missing fasteners.

parts.name: Propeller
parts.description: Two-blade metal propeller bolted to the crankshaft flange. Small nicks concentrate stress and can grow into fatigue cracks, so blades get a close visual inspection.

parts.name: Spinner
parts.description: Streamlined cover over the propeller hub. Its attaching screws, bulkhead and shell are checked for tightness and cracks.
